content.comment_body: Hello, When I attempted to print a Diagram using [product_name] V8.1, I switched the paper type from A3 to Tabloid. Afterward, the print preview displayed thousands of pages (specifically 9907) to print, and I am unsure why this happens. I have tested the diagram on several computers and all exhibit the same behavior, so I believe this is a program issue. Does anyone know how to resolve this? I've attached a screenshot showing how the program slices the diagram for printing. Thanks!

I've discovered what causes this issue, but not how to fix it. If you enter the Print Preview Properties, then change the zoom level (for example, from 50% to 75%), the diagram shrinks significantly. Changing the paper type from A3 to Tabloid in Page Setup then leads to thousands of pages being created for print (in one case, 4,829 pages).
I have the same printing issue. Adjusting the zoom from 25% in 1% increments helps a bit, but doesn't fully solve the problem.
Please update your [product_name] version to V8.2. This update should resolve the issue.
The [product_name] software should always be kept up to date with the latest upgrades. This is necessary to ensure compatibility with new device releases.

The issue is resolved now. The biggest challenge was locating the correct page since the simple 'update center' did not work. [url] However, I've encountered a new, minor bug: IO numbers on the printed list are now sorted alphabetically rather than numerically (e.g., I1, I10, I11, I2, I3), whereas in version 8.1, the sorting was correct.
This alphabetical sorting of IO numbers already existed in [product_name] V8.1.1.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face a severe printing problem in [product_name] V8.1, where changing paper and zoom settings causes the software to split diagrams across thousands of pages. The problem persists across different systems, indicating a software-level issue. Additionally, users notice after updates that IO numbers in printouts are sorted alphabetically, not numerically, which is a less critical but notable usability concern.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and dependable print settings, allowing for logical adjustment of paper format and zoom, resulting in an organized print output that accurately matches the diagram as viewed on screen.
